actions.lesson_title: Hedged 'likely to' needs a definite future outcome, not a tendency
actions.trigger: Gate FAIL on the Proposed text: canaries 83/83, Predictive +27.3 points (fixed 3, HOLD on a wide interval), but Hypothetical 81.8% to 63.6% with two regression cases (a scenario 'will' claim and a 'would' claim) sliding from apply to ask-editor, and the 'likely to expand' row sliding to ask-editor.

after.Editor wording: Fires on an unconditional future/forecast marker: will, is expected to, is forecasted to, is projected to, is set to ("the market is forecasted to grow to a multi-trillion size by 2030", "the largest wave of maturities is expected in the fall"). Hedged markers (is likely to, is likely, probably) fire only when they attach to a definite future outcome or event that only the future can settle ("the hiring freeze is likely a short-lived phase" fires). Hedged markers do NOT fire when they describe: an actor's general tendency or disposition, which can be checked against its past record ("the agency is likely to side with large incumbents"); a comparison of which strategy or approach tends to work better ("tariffs are more likely than talks to change the policy"); or a present trajectory ("is on track to", "is heading toward"). Such claims are assessments of the present, not forecasts. In particular, a hedged claim that an actor is likely to keep doing, continue or extend what it already does (to expand, tighten or favour something further), even with a future time phrase attached, describes that actor's tendency and does not fire. This rule decides Predictive only: it never decides whether a claim is Hypothetical, which Hypothetical's own rules settle unchanged, so a conditional or scenario claim keeps the Hypothetical verdict those rules give it even where this rule would also fire, and the two tags may stand together.

actions.note: Only the Editor wording property written; Status left Approved. Single paragraph, no leading '1.', no decided claim quoted verbatim, 1,439 characters.
